test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an iron-ore producing belt of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bilaspur-Panipat belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bilaspur-Panipat belt is **NOT an iron-ore producing region** in India.
 
• India’s major iron-ore producing belts are the **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt**, **Odisha-Jharkhand belt**, and **Maharashtra-Goa belt**.
 
• The **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt** in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra is known for its high-grade hematite ores, with major mines like Bailadila.
 
• The **Odisha-Jharkhand belt** includes key mines such as Barbil, Noamundi, and Gua, contributing significantly to India’s total iron ore output.
 
• The **Maharashtra-Goa belt** is famous for low-grade iron ore, with Goa playing a significant role in exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Ore in India:**

 
 
• Iron ore is a key raw material for steel production, with India being one of the largest producers globally.
 
• Major types of iron ore found in India include **hematite** (high-grade, widely used) and **magnetite** (low-grade).
 
 
 
• **Bailadila Mines:**
 
 
• Located in the Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt in Chhattisgarh.
 
• They produce some of the highest-grade hematite ore in India, which is used domestically and exported.
 
 
 
• **Odisha-Jharkhand Belt:**
 
 
• Odisha is India’s largest producer of iron ore, contributing around **50%** of the country’s total production.
 
• Keonjhar and Sundargarh districts are prominent mining regions.
 
 
 
• **Goa’s Contribution to Iron Ore:**
 
 
• Known for low-grade iron ore, which is primarily exported to countries like China and Japan.
 
• Mining activities in Goa have faced regulatory challenges in recent years.
